en: Mayon Volcano in Albay displays a nearly perfect, observable conical shape formed by alternating layers of solidified lava and ash.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River in Palawan flows directly into the sea, making its lower half subject to observable ocean tides.
Taal Lake in Batangas contains Volcano Island, which itself holds a smaller, observable crater lake visible during dry seasons.
The Rafflesia consanguinea, observable in Mount Kitanglad, produces massive, red, foul-smelling flowers that can reach 80 centimeters in diameter.
During the amihan season, the observable northeast monsoon brings cool, dry air to the Philippines, causing clear skies and lower humidity.
Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park in the Sulu Sea features massive, observable coral atolls that rise directly from deep ocean waters.
The Chocolate Hills in Bohol consist of over a thousand observable, cone-shaped limestone mounds that turn brown during the dry season.
Kawasan Falls in Cebu features observable, cascading turquoise water tiers formed by limestone rocks and underground river springs.
The Philippine Eagle, observable in the forests of Mindanao, possesses a distinct crest of dark brown feathers on its head.
The white sand of Boracay consists of finely crushed coral and shells, creating a noticeably bright and powdery texture on the beach.
Mount Pinatubo in Zambales contains a deep, observable crater lake that formed after the massive volcanic eruption in 1991.
The mangrove forests in Olango Island Wildlife Sanctuary feature observable, stilt-like root systems that allow trees to breathe in muddy tidal waters.
